title: the $125 Billion Secret: Amazon Told Wall Street One Thing and Employees Another. Here's the Truth.

hook_anatomy.first_5_seconds: Amazon is not cutting 30,000 jobs because they have too many managers, whatever they may say. They're cutting 30,000 jobs because they need the money to buy GPUs.
hook_anatomy.emotional_trigger: Skepticism and revelation - challenging official narrative with insider knowledge

act_breakdown.description: Challenge official narrative and present shocking claim
Present contradictory evidence - strong earnings vs massive layoffs
Deep dive into financial analysis - cash flow crisis revealed
Deconstruct CEO's culture narrative and reveal true motivations
Zoom out to industry-wide implications and future predictions

narrative_structure.payoff_delivery: Complete reframe of layoffs as capital reallocation, not culture problem

rhetorical_devices.example: Revenue hit $180 billion... And then they fired 30,000 people
Human headcount is being converted to compute capacity. Salaries are being transformed into silicon
Bigger than the moon race, bigger than the atom bomb

content_patterns.unique_angle: Financial detective work exposing gap between official narrative and balance sheet reality

key_quotes: Human headcount is being converted to compute capacity
This is not a layoff. This is a capital reallocation
You're not being replaced by an AI really, you're being replaced by the need to buy GPUs

analysis.one_line_summary: Amazon's 30,000 layoffs aren't about culture or efficiency—they're about converting human salaries into AI infrastructure spending as free cash flow turns negative.
